chunks: [A part of the same sermon — A caution:]

You should know that a man gets satiated and wearied with everything except life, because he does not find for himself any pleasure in death. It is in the position of life for a dead heart, sight for the blind eye, hearing for the deaf ear, quenching for the thirsty and it contains complete sufficiency and safety.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of 'life' versus 'death' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this sermon from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali contrasts the transient satiety of worldly pursuits with the enduring vitality of wisdom (al-hikmah), which he equates with true spiritual life. Drawing on Shia exegetical tradition, this passage underscores that wisdom acts as the animating force for the soul, offering permanence and peace where material existence offers only weariness. The metaphor of wisdom as sight for the blind and hearing for the deaf highlights its role in perceiving divine realities beyond the physical realm.
